## Problem 2

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_colour_viridis_d
scale_fill_discrete = scale_fill_viridis_d
```

Loading and cleaning the accelerometer dataset 

```{r}
nhanes_accel =
  read_csv(
    file = "data/nhanes_accel.csv",
    na = c("", "NA", ".")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
   pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440, 
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims") |>
      mutate (
      minute = as.numeric(minute))

nhanes_accel
```

Loading and cleaning the participants' demographic data

```{r}
nhanes_demo =
  read_csv(
    file = "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
    skip = 4, 
    na = c("", "NA", ".")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
  sex = recode_values(
    sex,
    1 ~ "male",
    2 ~ "female"),
  sex = factor(sex, levels = c("male", "female")),
  education = recode_values(
    education, 
    1 ~ "Less than high school",
    2 ~ "High school equivalent",
    3 ~ "More than high school"),
    education = factor(education, levels = c(
      "Less than high school",
      "High school equivalent",
      "More than high school"))) |>
  filter (
    age >= 21) |>
    drop_na()

nhanes_demo
```

Merging the datasets 

```{r}
nhanes_combined_df = 
  left_join(nhanes_demo, nhanes_accel, by = "seqn")

nhanes_combined_df
```

Making a table for the number of men and women in each education category

```{r}
nhanes_demo |>
  group_by(education) |>
  summarize(
    male = sum(sex == "male"),
    female = sum(sex == "female"),
    total = n()) |>
   knitr::kable(col.names = c("Education", "Men", "Women", "Total"))
```

Visualizing the age distributions for men and women in each education category

```{r}
nhanes_demo |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ education)
```

Description of the data: 

About half of participants (115 of 228) completed more than high school, while roughly one quarter completed less than high school (55) and one quarter completed a high school equivalent (58). Men and women are evenly distributed across education categories, except for the high school equivalent category, which includes more men than women (35 vs. 23). Age also varies by education level. Participants with less than a high school education are the oldest, with similar median ages for men and women (about 60). In the high school equivalent group, women are older than men (median about 62 vs. 53). Participants with more than a high school education are the youngest, with median ages around 41–43 for both sexes. Overall, median age decreases as education level increases

Creating a total activity variable for each participant

```{r}
nhanes_summed_mims =
  nhanes_combined_df |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  summarize(total_activity = sum(mims), .groups = "drop")

nhanes_summed_mims
```


```{r}
nhanes_summed_mims |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .3) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  scale_colour_hue(h = c(100, 300)) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Daily Activity by Age, Sex, and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex",
    caption = "Data from NHANES accelerometer study.")
```
Plot Description: 

Total daily activity generally declines with age, though the pattern differs by sex and education level. Among participants with less than a high school education, activity declines most steeply, from about 18,500 MIMS for women and 17,000 MIMS for men in their 20s to about 9,000 MIMS for both sexes by age 80. Women in this group are more active than men until about age 40, after which men are more active, rising from age 50 to a peak at 60 before declining again. In the high school equivalent group, women are more active than men through most of adulthood; activity rises for both sexes to a peak around age 40, then declines steadily, with a smaller second peak for women around age 70. Among participants with more than a high school education, activity is the most stable, remaining fairly level until about age 45 for men and age 60 for women before declining, and women are more active than men at nearly all ages. 

```{r}
nhanes_combined_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 360, 720, 1080, 1440),
    labels = c("12am", "6am", "12pm", "6pm", "12am")) +
  scale_colour_hue(h = c(100, 300)) +
  labs(
    title = "Smoothed 24-Hour Activity by Education Level",
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex",
    caption = "Data from NHANES accelerometer study.") +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"))
```



```{r}
nhanes_combined_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = seqn), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 360, 720, 1080, 1440),
    labels = c("12am", "6am", "12pm", "6pm", "12am")) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity by Education Level",
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex",
    caption = "Data from NHANES accelerometer study.") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"))
```
A.I Disclosure: used AI to figure out how to get my labels to stop overlapping (line X).

Plot Description: 

The timing of daily activity is similar across education levels and sexes, with only slight differences in activity level. It is lowest between about 3am and 5am, rises sharply between 6am and 10am, stays elevated through the afternoon, and declines in the evening around 7pm. Within each education level, the timing of daily activity for men and women are close. Women are slightly more active than men during the day in the high school equivalent and more than high school education groups, with the clearest difference in the more than high school group. In the less than high school group, men and women have similar daytime activity, but men are slightly more active around midnight and in the early morning. The more than high school group shows the most variation between individuals, with some participants reaching much higher activity levels.
